results.title: Test element

results.summary: An element $u$ of a group $G$ is a test element of $G$ if every endomorphism $\varphi$ of $G$ with $\varphi(u) = u$ is bijective, that is, an automorphism of $G$.

results.title: Bergman's question for three maximal subgroups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Kourovka 17.17 (G. M. Bergman) asks whether a finitely generated group with only finitely many maximal subgroups must be finite. This is the case of three maximal subgroups, which the problem singles out: every finitely generated group with exactly three maximal subgroups is finite.

results.title: Not every finitely generated group with three maximal subgroups is finite
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a finitely generated infinite group with exactly three maximal subgroups; that is, it is false that every finitely generated group with exactly three maximal subgroups is finite.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 15.32: large automorphisms and cyclic subgroups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For every prime $p$ and all natural numbers $k$ and $m$ with $m \ge 64k + 2$, every finite group $G$ of order $p^m$ that has an automorphism of order $p^{m-k}$ has a cyclic subgroup of index $p^k$.

results.title: Large automorphisms of p-groups force cyclic subgroups of given index
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every prime $p$ and all natural numbers $k$ and $m$ with $m \ge 64k + 2$, if a finite group $G$ of order $p^m$ has an automorphism of order $p^{m-k}$, then $G$ has a cyclic subgroup of index $p^k$.

results.title: Products of at most $n$ commutators (Kourovka 14.15)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $n$ a natural number. An element $z \in G$ is a product of at most $n$ commutators when there are $m \le n$ and elements $x_1, y_1, \dots, x_m, y_m \in G$ with $z = [x_1, y_1] \cdots [x_m, y_m]$, where $[x, y] = xyx^{-1}y^{-1}$; for $m = 0$ the empty product is the identity.

results.title: Unbounded commutator length in Aut(Fₙ) (Kourovka 14.15)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition that for every $n \ge 3$, writing $F_n$ for the free group on $n$ generators, and for every natural number $k$, some element of the derived subgroup of $\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)$ is not a product of at most $k$ commutators $xyx^{-1}y^{-1}$ of elements of $\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)$. This is the answer $k_n = \infty$ to Bardakov's question, which asks for the supremum $k_n$ of the commutator lengths of…

results.title: Commutator length in Aut(Fₙ) is unbounded
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n \ge 3$ and let $F_n$ be the free group on $n$ generators. For every natural number $k$ there is an element of the derived subgroup of $\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)$ that is not a product of at most $k$ commutators $xyx^{-1}y^{-1}$ with $x, y \in \operatorname{Aut}(F_n)$. Equivalently, the supremum $k_n$ of the commutator lengths of the elements of the derived subgroup of $\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)$ is infinite.

results.title: Products of a bounded number of commutators
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a group $G$, a natural number $m$ and $g \in G$, $g$ is a product of at most $m$ commutators when there are $k \le m$ and $a_1, b_1, \dots, a_k, b_k \in G$ with $g = [a_1, b_1] \cdots [a_k, b_k]$, where $[a, b] = aba^{-1}b^{-1}$; for $k = 0$ the empty product is the identity.

results.title: Commutator width of the derived subgroup
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a group $G$ with derived subgroup $G'$, the commutator width $w(G')$ is the least positive integer $m$ such that every element of $G'$ is a product of at most $m$ commutators $aba^{-1}b^{-1}$ with $a, b \in G$; it is $0$ when no such $m$ exists.

results.title: Bardakov's commutator width ratio claim (Kourovka 16.8)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition that for every finite non-abelian group $G$ the commutator width $w(G')$ of its derived subgroup $G'$ satisfies $w(G')/|G| \le 1/6$, and that for the symmetric group $S_3$ equality holds: $w(S_3')/|S_3| = 1/6$.

results.title: The maximal commutator width ratio is one sixth
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite non-abelian group $G$, the commutator width $w(G')$ of its derived subgroup satisfies $w(G')/|G| \le 1/6$, and for the symmetric group $S_3$ equality holds, $w(S_3')/|S_3| = 1/6$; so Kourovka Problem 16.8 has a positive answer.

results.title: Products of at most $n$ commutators
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An element $z$ of a group $G$ is a product of at most $n$ commutators when $z = [x_1, y_1] \cdots [x_k, y_k]$ for some $k \le n$ and some $x_1, y_1, \dots, x_k, y_k \in G$, where $[x, y] = x y x^{-1} y^{-1}$; for $k = 0$ the product is the identity.

results.title: Unbounded commutator length
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ has unbounded commutator length when for every natural number $n$ some element of the derived subgroup $[G, G]$ is not a product of at most $n$ commutators $x y x^{-1} y^{-1}$ with $x, y \in G$.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 14.13(a) (Bardakov)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that there is a simple group $G$ such that for every natural number $n$ some element of the derived subgroup $[G, G]$ is not a product of at most $n$ commutators $x y x^{-1} y^{-1}$ with $x, y \in G$.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 14.13(b) (Bardakov)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that there is a finitely presented simple group $G$ such that for every natural number $n$ some element of the derived subgroup $[G, G]$ is not a product of at most $n$ commutators $x y x^{-1} y^{-1}$ with $x, y \in G$.

results.title: A simple group with unbounded commutator length
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a simple group $G$ such that for every natural number $n$ some element of the derived subgroup $[G, G]$ is not a product of at most $n$ commutators $x y x^{-1} y^{-1}$ with $x, y \in G$. This answers Kourovka Problem 14.13(a) in the affirmative; the Kourovka Archive records examples constructed by Barge and Ghys, and finitely generated ones by Muranov.

results.title: A finitely presented simple group with unbounded commutator length
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a finitely presented simple group $G$ such that for every natural number $n$ some element of the derived subgroup $[G, G]$ is not a product of at most $n$ commutators $x y x^{-1} y^{-1}$ with $x, y \in G$. This answers Kourovka Problem 14.13(b) in the affirmative; the Kourovka Archive cites Caprace and Fujiwara.

results.title: Weak maximal condition on subgroups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ satisfies the weak maximal condition on subgroups when there is no infinite ascending chain $H_0 \le H_1 \le \cdots$ of subgroups of $G$ in which every index $|H_{i+1} : H_i|$ is infinite.

results.title: Weak minimal condition on subgroups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The weak minimal condition on subgroups: there is no infinite descending chain `H₀ ≥ H₁ ≥ ⋯` of subgroups with every index `|Hᵢ : Hᵢ₊₁|` infinite.

results.title: Minimal condition implies weak maximal condition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Kourovka 10.14(a) (D. I. Zaitsev): every group with the minimal condition on subgroups satisfies the weak maximal condition on subgroups.

results.title: Maximal condition implies weak minimal condition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Kourovka 10.14(b): every group with the maximal condition on subgroups satisfies the weak minimal condition on subgroups.

results.title: A group with the minimal condition can fail the weak maximal condition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a group $G$ satisfying the minimal condition on subgroups (there is no infinite strictly descending chain of subgroups of $G$) that has an infinite ascending chain $H_0 \le H_1 \le \cdots$ of subgroups in which every index $|H_{i+1} : H_i|$ is infinite. This answers Kourovka Problem 10.14(a) negatively.

results.title: A group with the maximal condition can fail the weak minimal condition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a group $G$ satisfying the maximal condition on subgroups (there is no infinite strictly ascending chain of subgroups of $G$) that has an infinite descending chain $H_0 \ge H_1 \ge \cdots$ of subgroups in which every index $|H_i : H_{i+1}|$ is infinite. This answers Kourovka Problem 10.14(b) negatively.

results.title: Length bound for progressions in a reduced residue window
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m$ be an integer and $n$ a natural number, and let $R_m(n)$ be the set of integers $a$ with $m + 1 \le a \le m + n$ and $\gcd(a, n) = 1$. If $b$ is an integer, $d$ a positive integer and $s$ a natural number such that $b + i d \in R_m(n)$ for every $0 \le i < s$, then $s \le n$.

results.title: The longest progression length is at most the modulus
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every integer $m$ and natural number $n$, $f_m(n) \le n$, where $f_m(n)$ is the length of the longest arithmetic progression with positive common difference contained in the set $R_m(n)$ of integers $a$ with $m + 1 \le a \le m + n$ and $\gcd(a, n) = 1$.

results.title: The reduced residue system $R_{-3}(5)$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The reduced residue system $R_{-3}(5)$ of the integers $a$ with $-2 \le a \le 2$ and $\gcd(a, 5) = 1$ is $\{-2, -1, 1, 2\}$: an integer $a$ lies in $R_{-3}(5)$ if and only if $a$ is one of $-2$, $-1$, $1$, $2$.

results.title: Longest progressions of absolute least residues modulo 5
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The length $g(5)$ of the longest arithmetic progression in the absolute least reduced residue system modulo $5$ is $2$.

results.title: Prime bound for progressions with a fixed difference
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m$ be an integer, $n > 1$ and $d > 0$ natural numbers, and $p$ a prime that divides $n$ but not $d$. Then $f_m(d, n) \le p - 1$, where $f_m(d, n)$ is the length of the longest arithmetic progression with common difference $d$ contained in the set $R_m(n)$ of integers $a$ with $m + 1 \le a \le m + n$ and $\gcd(a, n) = 1$.

results.title: Squarefree bound for progressions with a fixed difference
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m$ be an integer, $n > 1$ a squarefree natural number with largest prime factor $\operatorname{gpf}(n)$, and $d > 0$ a natural number. Then $f_m(d, n) \le \operatorname{gpf}(n) - 1$, where $f_m(d, n)$ is the length of the longest arithmetic progression with common difference $d$ contained in the set $R_m(n)$ of integers $a$ with $m + 1 \le a \le m + n$ and $\gcd(a, n) = 1$.

results.title: Longest progressions of absolute least residues: primes congruent to 1 mod 4
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a prime $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$, the length $g(p)$ of the longest arithmetic progression in the absolute least reduced residue system modulo $p$ is $(p - 1)/2$.

results.title: Longest progressions of absolute least residues: primes congruent to 3 mod 4
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a prime $p \equiv 3 \pmod 4$, the length $g(p)$ of the longest arithmetic progression in the absolute least reduced residue system modulo $p$ is $(p + 1)/2$.

results.title: Longest progressions of absolute least residues: prime powers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $r \ge 1$, with $r \ge 2$ when $p$ is odd. Then the length $g(p^r)$ of the longest arithmetic progression in the absolute least reduced residue system modulo $p^r$ is $p^{r-1}$.

results.title: Longest progressions of absolute least residues: odd squarefree composite moduli
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n > 1$ be an odd squarefree natural number that is not prime, let $P$ be its largest prime factor and $d = n / P$, and let $g(n)$ be the length of the longest arithmetic progression in the absolute least reduced residue system modulo $n$. Then $g(n) = \lfloor P - (P + 1)/(2d) \rfloor$.

results.title: Longest progressions of absolute least residues: twice an odd prime
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an odd prime $p$, the length $g(2p)$ of the longest arithmetic progression in the absolute least reduced residue system modulo $2p$ is $p - 1$.

results.title: Longest progressions of absolute least residues: neither squarefree nor prime power
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n > 1$ be a natural number that is neither squarefree nor a prime power, let $\operatorname{rad}(n)$ be the product of the distinct primes dividing $n$ and $P$ the largest prime factor of $n$, and let $g(n)$ be the length of the longest arithmetic progression in the absolute least reduced residue system modulo $n$. Then $g(n) = \max(n / \operatorname{rad}(n), P - 1)$.

results.title: Longest progressions of absolute least residues: even squarefree, three or more primes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ be an even squarefree natural number with at least three prime factors, let $P$ be its largest prime factor and $d = n / P$, and let $g(n)$ be the length of the longest arithmetic progression in the absolute least reduced residue system modulo $n$. Then $\lfloor P - 2P/d \rfloor \le g(n) \le P - 1$, and if $d \ge 2P$ then $g(n) = P - 1$.

results.title: $k$-generalized Lucas numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $k \ge 2$, the $k$-generalized Lucas numbers $L^{(k)}_n$ are the natural numbers indexed by the integers $n \ge 2 - k$ given by $L^{(k)}_n = 0$ for $2 - k \le n \le -1$, $L^{(k)}_0 = 2$, $L^{(k)}_1 = 1$, and $L^{(k)}_n = L^{(k)}_{n-1} + L^{(k)}_{n-2} + \dots + L^{(k)}_{n-k}$ for every integer $n \ge 2$. results.title: Hopf maximal ergodic theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mu$ be a finite measure on a measurable space $\alpha$, let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ preserve $\mu$, and let $f : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be measurable and $\mu$-integrable. For a natural number $n$ write $S_n f(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} f(T^k x)$. Then the integral of $f$ with respect to $\mu$ over the set of points $x \in \alpha$ such that $S_n f(x) > 0$ for some natural number $n$ is nonnegative.

results.title: Maximal divergence set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a measurable space, $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ a map, $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ a function and $c$ a real number. The maximal divergence set of $T$, $g$ and $c$ is the set of points $x \in \alpha$ for which there is a rational number $q > c$ such that $n q < \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} g(T^k x)$ for infinitely many natural numbers $n$.

results.title: Measurability of the maximal divergence set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$, let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ preserve $\mu$, and let $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be measurable. Then for every real number $c$, the maximal divergence set of $T$, $g$ and $c$ is a measurable set.

results.title: Membership in the maximal divergence set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a measurable space, $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ a map, $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ a function, $c$ a real number and $x \in \alpha$. Then $x$ lies in the maximal divergence set of $T$, $g$ and $c$ if and only if there is a rational number $q > c$ such that for every natural number $N$ there is a natural number $n \ge N$ with $n q < \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} g(T^k x)$.

results.title: Invariance of the maximal divergence set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a measurable space. For every map $T : \alpha \to \alpha$, every function $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ and every real number $c$, the preimage under $T$ of the maximal divergence set of $T$, $g$ and $c$ equals that set.

results.title: Invariance of the maximal divergence set under iterates
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a measurable space, $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ a map, $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ a function and $c$ a real number. For every natural number $k$ and every $x \in \alpha$, the point $T^k x$ lies in the maximal divergence set of $T$, $g$ and $c$ if and only if $x$ does.

results.title: Birkhoff pointwise ergodic theorem (ergodic case)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on a measurable space $\alpha$, let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ be ergodic with respect to $\mu$ (in particular $T$ preserves $\mu$), and let $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be $\mu$-integrable. Then for $\mu$-almost every $x \in \alpha$, the Birkhoff averages $\frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} g(T^k x)$ converge to $\int g \, d\mu$ as $n \to \infty$.

results.title: Integrability of Birkhoff sums
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$, let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ preserve $\mu$, and let $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be $\mu$-integrable. Then for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ the Birkhoff sum $x \mapsto \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} g(T^k x)$ is $\mu$-integrable.

results.title: Integrability of Birkhoff averages
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$, let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ preserve $\mu$, and let $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be $\mu$-integrable. Then for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ the Birkhoff average $x \mapsto \frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} g(T^k x)$ is $\mu$-integrable (for $n = 0$ it is the zero function).

results.title: Invariance of the integral under iterates
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$, let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ preserve $\mu$, and let $u : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be $\mu$-integrable. Then for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, writing $T^k$ for the $k$-th iterate of $T$, we have $\int u(T^k x) \, d\mu(x) = \int u \, d\mu$.

results.title: Birkhoff averages preserve the integral
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$, let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ preserve $\mu$, and let $u : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be $\mu$-integrable. Then for every $n \ge 1$, $\int \frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} u(T^k x) \, d\mu(x) = \int u \, d\mu$.

results.title: Triangle inequality for Birkhoff averages
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ be a map. For $f : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ and $n \ge 1$ write $A_n f(x) = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} f(T^k x)$ for the $n$-th Birkhoff average of $f$, and $A_0 f = 0$. Then for every $u : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$, every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every $x \in \alpha$, writing $|u|$ for the function $y \mapsto |u(y)|$, we have $|A_n u(x)| \le A_n |u|(x)$.

results.title: Monotonicity of Birkhoff averages
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ be a map. For $u : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$, $n \ge 1$ and $x \in \alpha$, write $A_n u(x) = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} u(T^k x)$ for the $n$-th Birkhoff average of $u$ at $x$, and $A_0 u(x) = 0$. If $u, v : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfy $u(y) \le v(y)$ for every $y \in \alpha$, then $A_n u(x) \le A_n v(x)$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every $x \in \alpha$.

results.title: Birkhoff averages of a bounded function are bounded
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ be a map, let $M \ge 0$, and let $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfy $|g(x)| \le M$ for every $x \in \alpha$. Then for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every $x \in \alpha$, the Birkhoff average $\frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} g(T^k x)$ (taken to be $0$ for $n = 0$) has absolute value at most $M$.

results.title: Birkhoff averages are $L^1$-contractions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$, let $T : \alpha \to \alpha$ preserve $\mu$, and let $g, h : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be $\mu$-integrable. For a function $f : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ and $n \ge 1$ write $A_n f(x) = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} f(T^k x)$, and $A_0 f = 0$. Then for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $\int |A_n g(x) - A_n h(x)| \, d\mu(x) \le \int |g(x) - h(x)| \, d\mu(x)$.

results.title: Classical pattern containment in a permutation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a permutation of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $\pi$ be a map from $\{0, 1, \dots, k-1\}$ to itself. Then $\sigma$ contains the pattern $\pi$ if there are positions $e_0 < e_1 < \dots < e_{k-1}$ in $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ such that for all $i, j < k$, $\sigma(e_i) < \sigma(e_j)$ holds exactly when $\pi(i) < \pi(j)$.

results.title: $K(d)$-families
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $n$, $k$ and $d$ be natural numbers and let $[n] = \{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$. A family $G$ of subsets of $[n]$ is a $K(d)$-family of $k$-subsets when every member of $G$ has exactly $k$ elements and any $d$ distinct members $A_1, \dots, A_d$ of $G$ with $|A_1 \cup \dots \cup A_d| \le 2k$ have a common element.

results.title: Mubayi's Erdős–Ko–Rado conjecture for $K(d)$-families

results.title: $s$-arc
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: Let $X$ be a finite graph and $s$ a natural number. An *$s$-arc* in $X$ is a sequence $(v_0, \dots, v_s)$ of vertices of $X$ such that $v_{i-1}$ and $v_i$ are adjacent for $1 \le i \le s$, and $v_{i-1} \ne v_{i+1}$ for $0 < i < s$.

results.title: $s$-arc transitive graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A finite graph $G$ is $s$-arc transitive if its automorphism group acts transitively on its $s$-arcs: for any two $s$-arcs $(u_0, \dots, u_s)$ and $(v_0, \dots, v_s)$ of $G$ there is an automorphism $\varphi$ of $G$ with $\varphi(u_i) = v_i$ for every $i \le s$.

results.title: $s$-arc regular graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A finite graph $G$ is $s$-arc regular if it has at least one $s$-arc and, for any two $s$-arcs $(u_0, \dots, u_s)$ and $(v_0, \dots, v_s)$ of $G$, there is exactly one automorphism $\varphi$ of $G$ with $\varphi(u_i) = v_i$ for every $i \le s$.

results.title: Base case of modular exponentiation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $a$ and $n$, modular exponentiation with base $a$, exponent $0$ and modulus $n$ returns $1$ and performs no multiplications.

results.title: Even step of modular exponentiation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $a$, $b$, $n$ be natural numbers with $b > 0$ and $b$ even. If modular exponentiation on base $a$, exponent $b/2$ and modulus $n$ returns the value $d$ using $t$ multiplications, then on base $a$, exponent $b$ and modulus $n$ it returns the value $(d \cdot d) \bmod n$ using $t + 1$ multiplications.

results.title: Odd step of modular exponentiation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $a$, $b$, $n$ be natural numbers with $b$ odd. If modular exponentiation on base $a$, exponent $b - 1$ and modulus $n$ returns the value $d$ using $t$ multiplications, then on base $a$, exponent $b$ and modulus $n$ it returns the value $(a \cdot d) \bmod n$ using $t + 1$ multiplications.

results.title: Modular exponentiation returns 1 at exponent zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $a$ and $n$, modular exponentiation with base $a$, exponent $0$ and modulus $n$ returns $1$.

results.title: No multiplications at exponent zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $a$ and $n$, modular exponentiation with base $a$, exponent $0$ and modulus $n$ performs no multiplications.

results.title: Value of the even step of modular exponentiation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $a$, $b$, $n$ be natural numbers with $b > 0$ and $b$ even, and let $d$ be the value returned by modular exponentiation on base $a$, exponent $b/2$ and modulus $n$. Then the value returned on base $a$, exponent $b$ and modulus $n$ is $(d \cdot d) \bmod n$.

results.title: Multiplication count in the even case
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $a$, $b$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $b$ positive and even. Modular exponentiation with base $a$, exponent $b$ and modulus $n$ performs exactly one more multiplication than it does with base $a$, exponent $b/2$ and modulus $n$.

results.title: Value of the odd step of modular exponentiation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $a$, $b$, $n$ be natural numbers with $b$ odd, and let $d$ be the value returned by modular exponentiation on base $a$, exponent $b - 1$ and modulus $n$. Then the value returned on base $a$, exponent $b$ and modulus $n$ is $(a \cdot d) \bmod n$.

results.title: Multiplication count in the odd case
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $a$, $b$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $b$ odd. Modular exponentiation with base $a$, exponent $b$ and modulus $n$ performs exactly one more multiplication than it does with base $a$, exponent $b - 1$ and modulus $n$.

results.title: Modular exponentiation is correct up to reduction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $a$, $b$, $n$ with $n > 0$, including $b = 0$, the value $r$ returned by modular exponentiation on base $a$, exponent $b$ and modulus $n$ satisfies $r \bmod n = a^b \bmod n$.

results.title: Modular exponentiation with a reduced base
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $a$, $b$, $n$ with $n > 0$, the value $r$ returned by modular exponentiation on base $a$, exponent $b$ and modulus $n$ satisfies $r \bmod n = (a \bmod n)^b \bmod n$.

results.title: Modular exponentiation returns a reduced value
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $a$, $b$, $n$ with $b > 0$, the value $r$ returned by modular exponentiation on base $a$, exponent $b$ and modulus $n$ satisfies $r \bmod n = r$ (with the convention $r \bmod 0 = r$).

results.title: Correctness of modular exponentiation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $a$, $b$, $n$ with $b > 0$ and $n > 0$, the value returned by modular exponentiation on base $a$, exponent $b$ and modulus $n$ equals $a^b \bmod n$.

results.title: Modular exponentiation returns a value below the modulus
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $a$, $b$, $n$ with $b > 0$ and $n > 0$, the value returned by modular exponentiation on base $a$, exponent $b$ and modulus $n$ is less than $n$.

results.title: Modular exponentiation returns the least residue
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $a$, $b$, $n$ with $b > 0$ and $n > 0$, the value $r$ returned by modular exponentiation on base $a$, exponent $b$ and modulus $n$ satisfies $r = a^b \bmod n$ and $r < n$.

results.title: Least residue at exponent zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $a$ and $n$ with $n > 1$, the value returned by modular exponentiation with base $a$, exponent $0$ and modulus $n$ equals $a^0 \bmod n$ and is less than $n$.

results.title: Unreduced result at modulus one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $a$, modular exponentiation with base $a$, exponent $0$ and modulus $1$ returns $1$, whereas $a^0 \bmod 1 = 0$.

results.title: The multiplication count depends only on the exponent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $a$, $a'$, $b$, $n$ and $n'$, modular exponentiation performs the same number of multiplications with base $a$, exponent $b$ and modulus $n$ as with base $a'$, exponent $b$ and modulus $n'$.

results.title: Multiplication count of modular exponentiation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $a$, $b$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $b > 0$, and let $\beta = \lfloor \log_2 b \rfloor + 1$ be the number of binary digits of $b$. The number of multiplications performed by modular exponentiation with base $a$, exponent $b$ and modulus $n$ is at least $\beta$ and at most $2\beta - 1$.
